text:
Predicates:
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
ComputerScienceDept(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x takes the database course.
InstructedBy(x, y) ::: x is instructed by y.
WorkingInLab(x) ::: x is working in the lab.
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
Premises:
¬∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x) → ComputerScienceDept(x)) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university are students who work in the library.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ TakesDatabaseCourse(x) → ComputerScienceDept(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ InstructedBy(x, david) → TakesDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorkingInLab(x) → InstructedBy(x, david)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
Student(james) ∧ WorkingInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬(PartTimeJob(jack) ∨ WorkingInLab(jack)) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.
Conclusion:
∀x (Student(james) ∧ PartTimeJob(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: James has a part-time job offered by the university.
